To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

vigorous recreational physical activity between ages 19 and > = 34 years was associated with a reduced risk of prostate cancer; recreational physical activity over the lifetime was not associated with prostate cancer risk; moderate-intensity recreational physical activities were not associated with the risks; weight training performed from early adult life onwards showed a non significant but consistent inverse association; and there was no strong evidence of a differential effect of physical activity on the risk of low-grade and high-grade prostate cancers.
